AC-45ARCH-05 · ARCH-06Same key/same payload, same key/different payload, crash before/after provider effect.Prior receipt reused or payload conflict returned; one accepted local outcome and truthful remote status.
AC-46SEC-02 · M2-05Wrong-tenant/site grant, unassigned site and API access to provisioner credentials.Selected resource access denied; privileged capability isolated; direct staff site-right limitation documented.
AC-47SEC-03 · UX-01Upload unsupported/oversized file, navigate stale link and edit during network/revision failure.Safe errors/limits; no untrusted preview execution or lost draft; keyboard/focus/status usable.
AC-48OPS-02 · OPS-04Run declared concurrent/import/report workload and cause sign, queue and backup failures.Agreed measured targets met or honestly failed; progress/telemetry/alerts identify operational owner.
AC-49OPS-01 · OPS-03Upgrade representative data and restore DB/documents/manifests in an isolated environment.Migration/rollback constraints documented; restore meets adopted RPO/RTO and validates hashes, totals and safe job recovery.
AC-50M1-01 · M1-02Duplicate client/profile merge proposal and revoked commercial recipient before dispatch.Authorized merge preserves history; revised recipient authority checked at send; no group-membership access shortcut.
AC-51CTRL-02 · UX-01Complete all ordinary tasks while payment, risk, evidence or professional gate remains blocked.Dashboard shows separate task progress/gate readiness and refuses direct lifecycle advancement.
AC-52M1-04 · M2-07 · M4-04Choose bookkeeping/AUP/internal-audit service without an approved applicable profile.Unsupported route clearly unavailable; never produce a fabricated statutory-audit opinion or gate bypass.
AC-53OPS-01 · ARCH-02Inspect release evidence for commit, lockfiles, migrations, full suites and real external checks.Same candidate traceable; fast CI/source presence do not substitute for release, provider or professional acceptance.
AC-54ARCH-01Submit forged role/gate values from the interface, request the same protected operation through an API and a worker, and inspect project dependencies.Server-owned authorization and invariants apply on every path; workers cannot invent human approval; domain calculation code has no HTTP, provider or database dependency.

Recommended delivery sequence

  1. Reconcile the contract. Inspect current repository instructions and behavior, adopt the source hierarchy, resolve D01–D10 only where they block the intended slice, and map revised IDs to actual owners. Do not replace working components because a historical document named them differently.
  2. Close authority and accounting foundations. Verify scope, source modes, reporting context, monetary invariants, transaction/idempotency rules and cross-artifact freshness. Add minimal schema constraints/migrations where evidence shows a gap.
  3. Complete one entity end to end. Implement an accepted TB through mapping, adjustments, all statements/notes, workprogram results, reviews, representations, signed report, fee note and five-part bundle.
  4. Complete existing alternate paths. Verify native bookkeeping cutover/close and group consolidation; keep unsupported profiles explicitly unavailable until accepted.
  5. Complete the operational handoffs. Finish commercial/finance reversals, task/calendar behavior, practice metrics, portal freeze, archive/corrections, provider reconciliation and coordinated recovery.
  6. Accept the release candidate. Run existing relevant tests first, add only targeted regression coverage for changed behavior, execute full required release gates on a pinned commit, then validate real external and professional acceptance separately.

Change discipline

Use small, independently reviewable stories under the existing module owner. Each story states verified current behavior, revised requirement IDs, minimal changed code/data/UI, denial/failure cases, migration impact and focused acceptance evidence. Avoid new abstractions, dependencies and broad refactors unless a measured problem requires them. Preserve existing data and issued artifacts. Actual merges or irreversible production actions remain subject to the repository's and user's designated authorization.

Overall completion criteria

  • Every retained baseline/current requirement and applicable workflow procedure has a source, owner and acceptance disposition; no approved ADR conflict is hidden.
  • Entity accounting, native-bookkeeping where enabled and group paths reconcile independently; firm and client financial domains remain separate.
  • Professional approvals, evidence, representations, output bytes, billing and release refer to the same current scoped versions.
  • Security covers all interactive, export, download and background surfaces; required external boundaries are observed rather than inferred.
  • The release candidate passes required application checks, genuine output-format checks, workflow demonstration, provider acceptance and restore objectives.
  • Remaining excluded/unsupported policies are visible to users and cannot silently produce a misleading approved report.

Decisions standards and source evidence

The design work is complete for review. The following policy choices need their named owners before the affected production behavior can be accepted. They do not require pausing implementation of unrelated, already-defined work.

DecisionRecommended resolutionOwner and safe rule until adopted
D01 Package and balance-invoice sequenceDefine financial-package publication separately from final client-bundle release; balance draft after published package and paid advance, finance approval/posting before bundle assembly.Engagement Partner + finance owner + technical owner. Preserve ADR-0007 and existing executed contracts; block ambiguous final bundles.
D02 Assembly clock retention and amendmentsAlign report/signature dates and assembly deadline under the applicable rules; approve retention/holds and supplementary correction/reissue procedure.Qualified audit/records owner. Keep the approved signature-based timer; flag earlier report-date deadline risk; no deletion or hidden reset.
D03 Service and reporting profilesApprove supported service routes, framework/edition/adoption, templates, disclosures and non-audit completion semantics; separate AUP from internal audit.Qualified audit/accounting owner. Unsupported combinations remain unavailable; never fake an audit approval/opinion.
D04 Materiality vocabulary and equalityDistinguish overall/performance/sample/trivial concepts. Recommend Red ≥PM, Amber ≥TE and <PM, with qualitative overrides; approve exact existing-compatible rule.Engagement methodology owner. Preserve current approved percentages, ±5% rounding, unnormalized PBT and risk overrides.
D05 Critical confirmation policyKeep the present stricter release gate. Only if the firm wants alternatives/opinion consequences to resolve a Critical case, adopt a precise reviewed policy.Qualified audit owner. Critical nonresponse remains blocked; no generic override or silent downgrade.
D06 Production signing assuranceDecide when certificate signing is mandatory and specify supported signature format, chain, expiry/revocation, validation, custody and legal acceptance.Firm signing authority + qualified legal/professional owner + security owner. Required missing or any configured unusable certificate blocks; optional unconfigured alone permits visual-only. No implied PAdES/LTV claim.
D07 Firm finance and metric policyConfirm advance recognition, credits/refunds/write-offs, revenue basis, actual-cost visibility and exact realization numerators, without changing accepted contracts.Finance owner. Preserve ADR-0018 and show missing rates/cost figures unavailable; no charge-out-as-profit display.
D08 External access and operating targetsAccept or explicitly narrow site-wide staff Full Control; agree production hosting/custody, provider permissions, load, RPO/RTO and acceptance owners.Firm owner + tenant administrator + operations/security owner. Preserve ADR-0006; no unverified external immutability or capacity claim.
D09 Quality-review applicabilityApprove required-engagement criteria, independent reviewer eligibility, evidence and sign-date gate inside existing governance/review.Firm quality-management owner. A required review without an eligible independent reviewer blocks signing.
D10 Supported consolidation casesApprove control/method, dates/policy alignment, acquisition/NCI/CTA treatment, FX rate bases and handling of complex ownership structures.Qualified group-reporting owner. Unsupported complex cases are explicit; no ownership-only or default-rate approximation.

Standards applicability that changes the design

Quality management: the IAASB identifies ISQM 1, ISQM 2 and ISA 220 (Revised) as replacing the old ISQC 1/ISA 220 framework, effective from 15 December 2022. Update current terminology while retaining historical source text. [R4]

Going concern: ISA 570 (Revised 2024) applies to audits of financial statements for periods beginning on or after 15 December 2026. Pin applicable editions rather than switching every 2026 engagement to the newest published text. [R6]

Financial statement presentation: IFRS 18 is effective for annual periods beginning on or after 1 January 2027, with earlier application permitted, and replaces IAS 1. This is a reporting-template/policy version within M4. Applicability also depends on the engagement's adopted framework and jurisdiction; do not retrofit a prior issued package. [R14]

Professional responsibility: a configured checklist, percentage, balanced equation, digital image or automated document cannot establish compliance on its own. The product must preserve human decisions and the supporting evidence. The workprogram source remains subject to professional tailoring.

Microsoft sign-in, scoped read, and protected command

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor User as Staff / client user
    participant UI as Angular browser
    participant API as ASP.NET Core API
    participant Entra as Microsoft Entra ID
    participant Actor as TrustedActorResolver
    participant App as Application command/query
    participant PG as PostgreSQL

    User->>UI: Open staff workbench or client portal
    UI->>API: Navigate /ui route / sign-in request
    API->>Entra: Server-side OIDC challenge
    Entra-->>API: Validated authentication callback
    API->>PG: Resolve/bind current identity and session
    API-->>UI: Secure HttpOnly cookie + XSRF cookie

    User->>UI: View client / engagement records
    UI->>API: GET same-origin /api/ui/* with cookie
    API->>Actor: Authenticate and resolve current actor
    Actor->>PG: Current user / firm / session epoch
    Actor-->>API: Scoped ActorContext or deny
    API->>App: Run named Application query
    App->>PG: Current RoleGrant + client/engagement scope checks
    alt Scope, current session and business read allowed
        PG-->>App: Current authorized records
        App-->>API: CommandResult<T> (exact decimals as strings)
        API->>Actor: Recheck session before emitting protected read
        API-->>UI: JSON response
    else Denied or stale
        App-->>API: Typed denial / stale result
        API-->>UI: Failure without unauthorized records
    end

    User->>UI: Submit draft or professional command
    UI->>API: POST /api/ui/* + cookie + XSRF header
    API->>API: Validate anti-CSRF and request limits
    API->>Actor: Resolve trusted actor again
    API->>App: Review exact command intent
    App->>PG: Lock in approved order; recheck role, scope, revision, independence
    alt Fully authorized current command
        App->>PG: Atomic business changes + immutable evidence/receipt
        App-->>API: Actor-owned outcome
        API-->>UI: Confirmed result
    else Denied or stale
        App-->>API: No publication; typed error
        API-->>UI: Denial / refresh-review prompt
    end

Interpretation / acceptance boundary: Every stage is computed from authoritative evidence, not assigned as an independent mutable status. Stage labels condense multiple exact gates; see source services for executable checks.

flowchart TB
    CLIENT["Client coordinator: authenticated first sign-in"] --> PBC["PBC request, upload chunk stream, versioned evidence"]
    PBC --> TRANSFER["Durable selected-site write + exact-version SHA readback"]
    TRANSFER --> REVIEW["Assigned reviewer accepts exact verified upload or rejects with reason"]
    REVIEW --> EVIDENCE["Immutable accepted source and provider receipt"]
    EVIDENCE --> WORKPAPER["Audit workpaper and current procedure evidence"]
    WORKPAPER --> GATE["Manager-reviewed work, SRM, critical confirmations"]
    GATE --> PARTNER["Staffed Partner selects opinion; modified basis if needed"]
    PARTNER --> SIGN{"Certificate required or configured?"}
    SIGN -->|"Optional unconfigured"| VISUAL["Visual Partner PNG + firm seal only; not cryptographic signature"]
    SIGN -->|"Required/configured"| CERT["Firm-held X.509 signing; validate key, dates, usage"]
    CERT --> CERTOK{"Credential usable?"}
    CERTOK -->|No| BLOCKSIGN["Fail closed: do not sign with image-only fallback"]
    CERTOK -->|Yes| PDFVERIFY["Sign exact PDF and verify embedded byte integrity;<br/>trust / revocation not asserted"]
    VISUAL --> BUNDLE
    PDFVERIFY --> BUNDLE["Five-part bundle: signed report/statements, management letter,<br/>signed LOR, correspondence, posted balance invoice"]
    FINPKG["Separately released reviewed financial package"] --> BALDRAFT["Balance-fee draft eligible after paid advance"]
    BALDRAFT --> BALPOST["Independent finance review and posted balance invoice"]
    BALPOST --> BUNDLE
    LOR["Client-signed LOR, human Partner-verified exact PDF"] --> BUNDLE
    FINPKG --> BUNDLE
    BUNDLE --> RELEASE["Authorized release, issued byte / manifest SHA identities"]
    RELEASE --> PORTAL["Client bundle availability, final-release PBC upload fence"]
    RELEASE --> STORE["Authoritative append-only platform release/archive store"]
    STORE --> COPY["Separate secondary SharePoint read-only library copy"]
    COPY --> PROTECT["Read back exact file hashes and expected access grants"]
    PROTECT --> EXT{"Remote state independently OBSERVED?"}
    EXT -->|No| BLOCKED["Provider BLOCKED_EXTERNAL; no immutability claim"]
    EXT -->|Yes| REPORTED["Report verified secondary-copy access only"]
    STORE --> CLOCK["Signature-anchored 60-day due date or earlier Partner lock"]
    CLOCK --> FREEZE["Commit local read-only freeze; append-only audit evidence"]
    FREEZE --> ARCHIVED["Derived ARCHIVED_READ_ONLY state"]

Interpretation / acceptance boundary: Do not infer cryptographic certificate trust, revocation or legal acceptance from byte integrity. Required defaults false unless explicitly configured. The independent release/archive store is authoritative; SharePoint copies do not offer admin-proof permanence. Final balance invoice may be prepared earlier under its own reviewed milestone and financial-package release gate.

Architecture / View 13

Durable local/outbound operations and unknown-outcome recovery

Operation intent / leased worker execution / verified remote effects / idempotent original-actor recovery.

Mermaid source preservedSnapshot a96c83d804ce
Mermaid source · Copy or export
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant UI as Angular user action
    participant API as ASP.NET Core API
    participant DB as PostgreSQL operations and receipts
    participant W as Group-isolated .NET Worker
    participant P as Configured provider or local effect

    UI->>API: Submit stable request identity + expected revision
    API->>DB: Validate scope and transactionally store intent + outbox row
    API-->>UI: Accepted request identity (not proof of provider success)
    W->>DB: Claim eligible row via SKIP LOCKED / lease + attempt token
    DB-->>W: Work item + current fence / capability metadata
    W->>DB: Revalidate current authority, generation and target identity
    alt Local operation
        W->>DB: Publish transaction-owned result + immutable receipt
    else External operation allowed + live prerequisite verified
        W->>P: Execute exact scoped operation
        alt Verified success
            P-->>W: Identity, version and provider receipt
            W->>P: Read back exact target / hash / grants
            P-->>W: Verification response
            W->>DB: Persist result and provider evidence; bind locally
        else Network timeout or result unknown
            W->>DB: Mark UNKNOWN / reconciliation-needed state
            W->>P: Read-only reconciliation of exact original request
            alt Observed original effect
                P-->>W: Exact original target and receipt
                W->>DB: Verify and publish original result
            else Absent or unprovable
                W->>DB: Keep blocked/unknown outcome; no blind duplicate create
            end
        end
    end
    UI->>API: Lookup original actor-owned receipt / request
    API->>DB: Recheck current scope and retained outcome
    DB-->>API: Original outcome or explicit pending/blocked state
    API-->>UI: Truthful recovery; never synthesize an approval
Related source sectionsv2.2 workflow requirements13 historical controls

These links provide topic navigation, not verified requirement-by-requirement implementation coverage.

Interpretation / acceptance boundary: Illustrates the general durable-operation contract; specific handlers define their own states, scopes, leases, and external evidence. Do not treat all Graph operations as retry-safe on timeout.

        DB[("PostgreSQL 18.6; migrations and backups")]

    end

    SECRETS --> LIVE

Approved deviations

The entries below are operative decision overlays, and the source requirements that follow are preserved for provenance. The approved or accepted decision records here control current interpretation where source prose differs; a decision does not prove implementation, live-provider acceptance or qualified professional treatment. Do not rewrite an executed client contract or infer a professional decision from this specification.

  • ADR-0002 (Angular canonical UI): Angular 22 is the canonical user interface. The Blazor rollback host was retired by owner decision and merged as e7ebe27c; retirement does not mean migration parity or rollback acceptance was established. Affects the header architecture row.
  • ADR-0003 (Microsoft sign-in for the client portal): no temporary passwords are emailed or stored; the first-sign-in requirement of the Microsoft identity path applies. For newly converted clients, portal access also requires both keys, activation and the paid advance. Live tenant acceptance remains separate. Affects the §3.1 portal box and the §4.1.5 portal bullets.
  • ADR-0004 (lifecycle as a derived projection): the §5 stages are computed from gate records and never stored or set directly. Affects §5.
  • ADR-0005 and ADR-0016 (visual appearance and certificate signing): the PNG signature and seal remain the visible appearance. A firm-held X.509 certificate can sign the final report; when certificate signing is required, missing or invalid certificate material fails closed with no image-only fallback. eSignature providers and Purview remain out of scope. The firm's real-certificate and legal acceptance, and whether production must require certificate signing, remain separate gates. Affects §4.1.4 and §§4.4.1–4.4.2.
  • ADR-0006 (one SharePoint site per client; Full Control for assigned staff): the site and staff-access decision does not establish archive immutability or provider read-only protection. The archive-copy rule is controlled by ADR-0009 below.
  • ADR-0007 (approved 50/50 fee milestones and draft-only automation): the gated engagement letter creates the reviewed fee agreement and its advance and balance milestones. Optional automation is off by default and creates invoice drafts only: the advance draft is eligible after the letter; the balance draft is eligible only after the advance is paid and the linked financial package is released. A draft is not approved, posted, sent or collected. A draft-report date alone is not the balance-invoice trigger. Preserve the terms and evidence of already accepted or executed contracts. Affects §§3.1, 3.4, 4.1.2, 4.1.5 and 4.4.2.
  • ADR-0009 (archive authority, from spike SPK-01): the append-only release and archive store is authoritative for issued evidence. A separate read-only SharePoint archive library is a secondary copy. Its state is OBSERVED only after both exact file hashes and expected grants are read back; until then it remains BLOCKED_EXTERNAL. A local freeze does not protect the SharePoint copy, and the UI or regulator export must not claim provider immutability. Affects §4.4.3.
  • ADR-0010 (end-of-service accrual, from STE-NXT-009): end-of-service benefits are accrued as a provision entered by a person, not expensed only when paid. Affects §3.5.
  • ADR-0011 and ADR-0017 (materiality without normalization): the PBT benchmark is mapped balances excluding tax; no normalization adjustments are applied. Affects §4.2.4.
  • ADR-0012 (unconditional advance activation gate; ACCEPTED): activation into PORTAL_ACTIVE_PLANNING requires a linked fee agreement and its 50% ADVANCE milestone in PAID state, representing full payment and allocation. No configuration bypass is permitted. An invoice, partial payment or missing agreement is insufficient. This does not retroactively change an executed contract. Affects §§4.1.5 and 5.1.
  • ADR-0017 (STE v2.2 delegated product decisions): WhatsApp is a lead-channel label only; nothing is ingested from or sent through it, and proposals are dispatched by email. Acceptance records EMAIL, SIGNED_LETTER, IN_PERSON or PHONE (required for acceptance, optional for decline); the value labels evidence and sends nothing. Add continuance questions RV-031 (legal notice, claim or demand received; adverse when yes) and RV-032 (prior-year professional fees settled; adverse when no), preserving existing questions and historical answers. The firm week is Sunday–Thursday with Friday/Saturday as weekend and Sunday–Saturday allocation weeks; public holidays are recorded as unavailability, with no inferred holiday table, and statutory-relative milestone dates remain the rule (the dates in the source are examples). The staffed Engagement Partner is required for SRM clearance, opinion, report signing, signed-representation verification and bundle assembly. Planning approval covers current materiality and risk routing; a recorded critical-estimate flag bands Red; high inherent risk is likelihood 3 with magnitude at least 2; Amber work is performed by Senior Auditor or above and reviewed by an Audit Manager. Sampling versus full-population testing is documented senior judgment; no sample is universally required. Affects §§3.1–3.5, 4.1–4.3, 5.1–5.2 and 6.3.
  • ADR-0018 (practice reporting bases): approved non-billable/no-charge time counts in actual hours and cost but has no charge-out value; standard value, realization and contract contribution use approved billable time only, and missing rate/currency makes those figures unavailable. Utilization is approved billable minutes divided by capacity net of recorded unavailability; show all approved hours separately. Age every posted firm invoice (advance, final, time or other); do not include client-bookkeeping invoices, and refuse a report for an invoice bound to multiple milestones. Monthly P&L uses one row per accounting month and the same month one year earlier as comparator. The dashboard names currently staffed users at the level owning each step but grants no permissions. Apply Senior/Supervisor/Junior/Associate rate aliases wherever rates are looked up. Staff-level performance measures and visibility, facility/benefit expense taxonomy, broader fee/partial-payment policy and the professional/legal items listed in ADR-0018 remain undecided. Affects §§3.5 and 4.5.1–4.5.2.
Source: Current STE v2.2 requirements · L491-L548 ↗

4.1.3 Dual-Key Onboarding Gatekeeper

The system shall strictly disallow the generation of an Engagement Letter until two independent authorization keys are marked active in the database:

  • Key 1 (Commercial Approval): Recorded confirmation of client quote acceptance.
  • Key 2 (Risk Clearance): Partner completion and digital sign-off of the Client Acceptance/Continuance Checklist (ISA 220).

Enhanced Dual-Key Acceptance — mandatory workflow requirements for version 2.2

Approval decision matrix

Key 1: client commercial acceptance Key 2: Partner risk clearance Engagement Letter Planning activation
Missing Missing Blocked Blocked
Approved Missing or stale Blocked Blocked
Missing or stale Approved Blocked Blocked
Current and valid Current and unconditional Eligible for separately authorized issuance Blocked until 50% advance is fully paid and allocated
Current and valid Current and unconditional; 50% advance allocated Eligible for separately authorized issuance Eligible, subject to other holds and authorization checks

Actor sequence

sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant CRM as Commercial Workspace
    participant Partner
    participant Risk as Acceptance Records
    participant Docs as Engagement Documents
    participant Finance
    participant Planning
    Client->>CRM: Accept exact dispatched quotation revision
    CRM->>Risk: Persist commercial response evidence
    Partner->>Risk: Review AML, KYC, independence and continuance
    Partner->>Risk: Record current risk decision
    CRM->>Risk: Recheck both independent approval keys
    alt Both keys current and approved
        Risk-->>Docs: Engagement Letter generation eligible
        Docs->>Finance: Initiate 50 percent advance fee workflow
        Finance->>Finance: Record and allocate payment
        alt Advance fully paid and no outstanding hold
            Finance-->>Planning: Activation may proceed through authorized command
        else Unpaid, partial, stale or held
            Finance-->>Planning: Activation blocked with exact reasons
        end
    else Missing or invalid approval
        Risk-->>CRM: Block document — show missing or stale key
    end
  • Key 1 — Client Commercial Acceptance: Capture the client's acceptance of the exact dispatched quotation revision, scope, legal entity, service route, period, currency, fee and 50/50 payment terms. Record authorized contact, response channel, timestamp and linked acceptance evidence. A changed offer requires a renewed acceptance.
  • Key 2 — Partner Risk Clearance: Independently require the Engagement Partner's current, unconditional client acceptance/continuance decision against the current due-diligence generation. Require AML/KYC, beneficial ownership, independence, conflicts, management integrity and other relevant risk checks. Conditional, rejected, superseded or stale decisions never clear this key.
  • Gate outcomes: neither key ⇒ blocked, two approvals needed; only Key 1 ⇒ awaiting Partner risk clearance; only Key 2 ⇒ awaiting client commercial acceptance; both current keys ⇒ eligible for Engagement Letter, NOT automatically activated.
  • The full 50% advance payment is a separate gate after the two keys: generate the Engagement Letter and advance invoice under their existing authorization rules; activate engagement and portal-enabled planning only after the linked 50% advance is fully paid and allocated. A partially paid or merely invoiced advance is not sufficient.
  • Changes and exceptions: a declined proposal returns to revision/re-dispatch or closure; a conditional or refused Partner decision returns to risk remediation and fresh unconditional review; open holds, stale commercial revisions and mismatched client/service scopes block protected operations. Never let task completion, workflow rules or staff overrides bypass these guards.
  • Onboarding interface: provide two independent approval cards, each showing Pending, Awaiting Evidence, Approved, Rejected or Stale as applicable, owner, time, evidence link, revision and authorized next action. Show a separate Engagement Letter readiness row and a third 50% Advance Payment card. Hide sensitive AML/KYC findings from the client portal.
  • Audit history: preserve the authentic approving actor, decision generation, source evidence, timestamps and reason for rejection; re-evaluate both keys at document generation and activation, and reject stale or concurrently changed inputs.
  • Worked example: on an accepted QAR 20,000 quotation, Partner acceptance is still mandatory before an Engagement Letter may be issued. Both keys permit letter issuance and the QAR 10,000 advance invoice, but activation waits until the full QAR 10,000 is received and allocated.

Implementation note: the unconditional 50% advance activation gate is recorded in ADR-0012. The matrix describes required behaviour; it does not by itself prove it. Verification status is in the v2.2 delta of the gap-verification tracker.

5.3 Display Phases and Canonical States

The eleven canonical states in §5.1 remain authoritative. Sections 6 and 7 present a simpler seven-phase user-facing workflow but do not replace these gate conditions. The diagram in §5.2 is not itself a permission model: transitions follow their underlying business commands and evidentiary gates.

Display phase Canonical states represented
1. Client Onboarding LEAD_INGESTION, PROPOSAL_GENERATION, DUAL_KEY_PENDING, ADVANCE_BILLING
2. Audit Planning PORTAL_ACTIVE_PLANNING
3. Audit Fieldwork FIELDWORK_EXECUTION
4. Manager Review MANAGERIAL_REVIEW
5. Partner Sign-off PARTNER_APPROVAL
6. Report and Delivery DELIVERABLE_RELEASE
7. Archive and Close COMPLIANCE_COUNTDOWN, ARCHIVED_READ_ONLY

6. Simplified Seven-Phase Engagement Workflow — New Requirements

6.1 Purpose and mapping

This user-interface and task orchestration layer SHALL NOT modify the canonical Section 5 lifecycle state names, stage gates, reviews, or compliance evidence. Map stages as follows:

  • Phase 1 Client Onboarding: LEAD_INGESTION, PROPOSAL_GENERATION, DUAL_KEY_PENDING, ADVANCE_BILLING.
  • Phase 2 Audit Planning: PORTAL_ACTIVE_PLANNING.
  • Phase 3 Audit Fieldwork: FIELDWORK_EXECUTION.
  • Phase 4 Manager Review: MANAGERIAL_REVIEW, with procedure-level rework loop back to affected fieldwork.
  • Phase 5 Partner Sign-off: PARTNER_APPROVAL.
  • Phase 6 Report & Delivery: DELIVERABLE_RELEASE.
  • Phase 7 Archive & Close: COMPLIANCE_COUNTDOWN and ARCHIVED_READ_ONLY.

6.2 Engagement dashboard

Show a seven-step visual tracker with simple titles, responsible user, relevant milestone/date, task completion, gate readiness, explicit blockers and the next permitted action. Offer expandable phase checklists and contextual links to client, planning, financial statement line item, PBC, review, completion, finance and records workbenches. Distinguish task completion from regulatory clearance. Make the design responsive and keyboard accessible.

6.3 Phase detail requirements

  • Client Onboarding: quotation and client response, separated dual-key approvals, Engagement Letter, 50% invoice/payment and activation eligibility.
  • Audit Planning: staff and deadlines, workspace provisioning, TB import, approved mapping, materiality PM/TE/SAD, risk routing and Partner planning approval. Updated inputs must invalidate stale approvals.
  • Audit Fieldwork: FSLI action links, workprograms, evidence, analytical reviews, sampling, preparer assignments and versioned result submission.
  • Manager Review: independent reviewer authority and risk-based hierarchy; mandatory comments on rejection; preserve history and route affected work back to its preparer; resolve all relevant review notes; compile a current SRM.
  • Partner Sign-off: review high-risk areas/SRM, select an ISA opinion and rationale when modified, and sign the final report under approved credentials.
  • Report & Delivery: independently evaluated critical confirmations, controlled audited statement and report delivery, management letter, LOR, correspondence, final fee note and release checkpoints.
  • Archive & Close: signature-anchored 60-day countdown, authorized early lock and effective local read-only freeze. Show external provider retention/protection independently; an expired timer alone is not archive success.

6.4 Reusable practice templates

Permit administrator-approved versioned templates by engagement type and industry, with editable task groups, owners, due-date offsets, dependencies, effort estimates, client requests and ad-hoc tasks. Pin a template revision to each engagement; changes to templates do not silently rewrite existing work. These templates cannot remove mandatory domain gates. Provide My Tasks, Team Work, Waiting for Client, Under Review, Rework, Overdue and Completed list filters plus Kanban/calendar views.

6.5 Recurring audit engagements

Support creating the next annual engagement with reusable templates, prior-year client details and historical mapping suggestions. Require fresh commercial consent, current Partner continuance risk approval, current TB/materiality, professional audit review and reporting decisions. Never carry prior-year acceptance or opinion sign-offs forward as valid authorization.

6.6 Safe workflow automation

Mermaid source · Copy or export
flowchart LR
    T["Versioned task template"] --> RUN["Engagement task instances"]
    RUN --> AUTO["Task automator"]
    AUTO --> GOOD["Permitted: assignments, follow-ups, reminders and escalation"]
    AUTO --> G{"Needs protected professional or financial decision?"}
    G -->|"Yes"| C["Submit to authorized domain command and independent actor"]
    G -->|"No"| GOOD
    C --> V["Check role, client scope, evidence and current revision"]
    V --> E["Persist authentic decision and audit event"]
    E --> PROJ["Recompute canonical lifecycle projection"]
    classDef decision fill:#fff1d6,stroke:#b88b2c,color:#5d4316
    class G decision

Automators MAY assign tasks, create follow-up checklists, set reminders and due dates, escalate overdue PBC requests and notify permitted users after genuine domain events. They SHALL NOT synthesize approvals, record payment, clear risk, approve materiality, sign an opinion, post invoices, issue release or freeze files. Every automation must reauthorize, use idempotency keys, pin current versions, log its changes and fail safely on stale inputs. Task graphs must reject dependency cycles.

6.7 User role, security and progress rules

Preparer sees assigned fieldwork/rework; Reviewer sees submissions and review notes; Partner sees acceptance, high-risk areas, opinion and release; Client sees only authorized commercial and PBC status. Calculate phase readiness from server-side records, not mutable task flags. Track task percentage separately from mandatory gate satisfaction, avoid leaking AML/KYC evidence to client users and show readable blocker reasons.

6.8 Acceptance criteria

Acceptance criteria to verify:

  1. All 11 canonical states map to exactly one of seven phases.
  2. Absent/one-key approvals block Engagement Letter issuance.
  3. Both keys allow the letter but do not bypass the full 50% advance.
  4. Changed offer or risk basis invalidates the affected approval.
  5. Rejection/conditional clearance and open holds cannot be overwritten through tasks.
  6. Independent reviewer and mandatory rework comments remain enforced.
  7. Open review notes and stale materiality block subsequent professional decisions.
  8. Critical confirmation cases block report release.
  9. Frozen archival state requires an effective committed lock and does not imply external immutability.
  10. Recurring templates never copy professional sign-offs as current.
  11. Scoped actors cannot access unrelated clients.
  12. Automation retries cannot duplicate or forge domain events.

7. Architectural Non-Regression Requirements — New

All domain commands and evidence records remain the sole authority for progression. The existing 11-stage derived lifecycle and five function modules remain unchanged. The seven-phase user experience is a deterministic presentation mapping. Task templates, personal work queues, recurring-engagement creation, deadline automation and dashboard analytics are separate supporting capabilities. All permissions, professional judgments, signed document integrity, 50/50 commercial terms and archive protections must continue to be enforced by authoritative services. Review external Microsoft identity/SharePoint/records protections separately before labelling them production compliant.

Original user personas

PREPARER

Audit Associate / Junior Auditor

  • Executes assigned financial statement line item (FSLI) audit test procedures.
  • Uploads digital working papers and inputs physical binder index codes (X-1, Box 3).
  • Submits completed testing packages for managerial review.
  • Logs daily operational hours against assigned engagement tasks.
Read current overlays
REVIEWER

Audit Senior / Audit Manager

  • Verifies substantive testing and recalculated schedules.
  • Issues inline review notes and initiates the rework loop for incomplete tests.
  • Determines sampling parameters and calculates engagement materiality.
  • Prepares the Summary Review Memorandum (SRM) for the partner.
  • Tracks engagement budgets, team hours, and delivery milestones.
Read current overlays
APPROVER

Engagement Partner

  • Evaluates and signs off on the Dual-Key Acceptance Gate (AML/KYC).
  • Authorizes commercial proposals and executes Engagement Letters.
  • Clears high-risk (Red) audit areas and formally signs off on the SRM.
  • Selects the final Audit Opinion, applies digital signatures and firm seals.
  • Authorizes final deliverable bundles and enforces regulatory file locks.
Read current overlays
CLIENT

Client Coordinator / CFO / MD

  • Accesses an isolated, tokenized external workspace (PBC Portal).
  • Views requested audit documentation with real-time review status badges.
  • Uploads requested financial schedules, trial balances, and voucher evidence.
  • Receives invoices, receipts, holding letters, and final deliverables.
  • Access freezes automatically upon engagement sign-off.

Codebase-review findings

The prior review is included in full. Its tests and observations belong to the recorded repository snapshot and review scope; packaging them here is not a new codebase audit.

This HTML changes presentation and navigation only. It does not close any codebase finding, approve an implementation, or replace the authority hierarchy in the repository.

AuditSphere: Updated HTML Documents versus Actual Repository

Review date: 18 October 2026
Inspected repository: nirzaf/AuditSphere
Inspected master snapshot: a96c83d804cecd39ca96a0bbbb7fb8ae4557be30
Disposition: Changes required before these documents are accepted as a current, code-aligned implementation reference.

Executive conclusion

The update substantially improves preservation and navigation, but it does not establish complete requirements coverage or trustworthy code traceability. All 115 historical statement IDs and normalized visible wording are preserved. The two new matrices contain the same 138 rows. Nevertheless, several concrete enforcement references cannot be found in application source, 104 acceptance criteria merely refer back to their requirements, approved-but-unimplemented work is presented as implemented, and important security and workflow descriptions contradict source.

These are principally documentation defects, not proof that the corresponding application capabilities are missing. Do not create duplicate services, alter correct HTTP contracts, broaden Microsoft permissions, or weaken financial gates merely to make the application match an incorrect diagram.

Review boundary

This was a read-only source review of the two uploaded HTML files, their earlier supplied versions, current authority documents, and targeted application, API, Domain, Infrastructure and Angular source. All repository file reads were pinned to the snapshot above. Repository searches that identified absent symbols were scoped to src/; the retrieved search results reported no incomplete results. Search results are not a substitute for a compiled symbol index.

All 138 document rows were compared mechanically. Selected high-risk behaviors were traced in code. This was not an executed end-to-end acceptance assessment of all 138 rows or an exhaustive functional/security audit of the repository. The original Word baseline was not independently revalidated. No application files, migrations, tenant resources, or deployments were changed. No application build or test suite was run.

Requirements-to-workflow references 138/138 match valid JavaScript tab route keys Canonical filenames assumed; not 138 missing DOM anchors
Workflow-to-Requirements references 175/175 target existing anchors Canonical filenames assumed

All 23 extension rows carry “Verified in design”. The evidence inspected does not support blanket acceptance of that status.

Findings

F01 — High: Concrete enforcement references do not match source

Document evidence: both matrices, including M1.02-R01, M1.03-R01 and EXT-ACC-01. In the uploaded workflow these rows start around lines 2150, 2227 and 3349 respectively; in Requirements around 3953, 4030 and 5152.

The following types had zero matches in repository searches scoped to src:

  • ProposalCompilationService, named as ProposalCompilationService.GenerateProposalAsync.
  • DualKeyAcceptanceService, named as DualKeyAcceptanceService.SignKeyAsync.
  • ClientAccountingProfileService, named as ClientAccountingProfileService.ActivateContextAsync.

Actual quotation and letter behavior is in src/AuditSphereOps.Application/Practice/CommercialDocumentService.cs. GenerateBriefQuotationAsync and GenerateEngagementLetterAsync delegate to GenerateDocumentAsync. Letter generation checks the approved quotation, current commercial acceptance, exact dispatch/response evidence, current unconditional Partner risk acceptance and source generation. Its risk evidence is resolved through EngagementRiskEvidence.ForPeriodAsync.

Correction: replace these references with the actual path and method chain, or explicitly label a reference as a proposed design element. Audit every remaining enforcement reference rather than assuming that plausible class names exist. An absent named type does not establish absence of the business capability.

F02 — High: The 138-row denominator omits material current requirements

The files preserve 115 historical statements and add 23 broad extension summaries. That is a document inventory, not a demonstrated inventory of all applicable current requirements.

docs/requirements/auditsphere-accounting-module-requirements-current.md is CURRENT v2.2 and explicitly adds the seven-phase workflow experience, phase-to-canonical-state mapping, engagement dashboards, reusable templates, recurring engagements, safe automation and security/non-regression rules. The revised HTML does not model that required seven-phase orchestration layer with its own traceable requirements and controls.

This is not merely speculative future functionality. src/AuditSphereOps.Application/Practice/EngagementWorkflowPlanService.cs contains published-template selection, preview and execution contracts, expected preview digests, idempotency keys, owner selections and typed PBC steps. Its explicit boundary is that templates create supporting tasks and fresh unsent PBC drafts; they do not advance the lifecycle or professional decisions.

The current requirement set also distinguishes authorized native bookkeeping from import-first accounting and requires reviewed cutover. The 23 extension summaries do not provide a complete mapping of those source-mode, invoice, credit, opening-balance and settlement workflows. This observation does not assert that every proposed bookkeeping feature is already mandatory or complete.

Correction: derive the applicable inventory from current normative sources and approved decisions, not a chosen number of extension summaries. Keep the historical 115 count separately. Do not announce a new “100%” denominator before the inventory and exclusions are complete.

F03 — High: Approved reporting-context design is presented as implemented

The accounting diagram immediately binds an ADR-0015 reporting-context revision. EXT-ACC-01 says context activation is verified and names the nonexistent service in F01. Requirements' extension narrative also says the accounting capabilities are fully implemented.

At the inspected snapshot, docs/architecture/adr/auditsphere-architecture-adr-0015-reporting-context-identity-pins-approved.md explicitly records T014 as unstarted and dependent on T013 and T007. Existing records already enforce scoped identities and selected revision pins; that is not proof that the complete new context-activation capability exists.

docs/execution/status.json separately records partial implementation/acceptance, false production enablement, and open financial-statement, parity and external gates. Historical slice evidence is not current whole-product acceptance.

Correction: distinguish approved target behavior, existing narrower safeguards, incomplete implementation and acceptance evidence. Remove unqualified “fully implemented” statements. Do not imply that an approved ADR itself proves implementation.

F04 — High: Archive acceptance invents a state and a universal HTTP contract

EXT-SEC-04 states that the engagement becomes ARCHIVED_LOCKED and that all POST/PUT/DELETE commands return HTTP 423. This conflicts with both files' own eleven-state register.

Actual source: src/AuditSphereOps.Application/Acceptance/EngagementLifecycleQuery.cs defines CanonicalEngagementStages.ArchivedReadOnly = "ARCHIVED_READ_ONLY". It derives this state from a committed local freeze; elapsed time alone is not an archived state. Local freeze and provider protection are exposed separately.

The shared command mapping in src/AuditSphereOps.Api/Ui/UiEndpoints.Infrastructure.cs uses typed errors mapped through StatusFor, including 401, 403, 409 and a 400 fallback. It does not implement the documented blanket 423 mapping.

Correction: use the canonical derived state and distinguish scheduled, overdue-but-not-committed, locally frozen and externally verified protection. Map each relevant denial to the existing route's actual error/status contract; do not mandate an undocumented global status-code rewrite.

F05 — High: Signature guarantees exceed the implementation

EXT-SEC-03 names PdfDigitalSigningService, claims certificate revocation checking, and states that a missing certificate always blocks signing. Requirements' ADR summary similarly states an unconditional missing-certificate failure.

Actual src/AuditSphereOps.Application/Completion/ReportCertificateSigning.cs implements:

  • Resolve: no configured certificate and signing not required permits visual signature/seal only.
  • Required-but-missing or configured-but-unusable certificate material blocks signing.
  • Validate: private key, validity interval, RSA key size and key-usage checks.
  • ReportSignatureVerifier.Verify: SignedCms.CheckSignature(verifySignatureOnly: true) verifies the signed bytes; it does not establish certificate trust or revocation status.

src/AuditSphereOps.Application/Completion/AuditDeliverableService.cs owns SignIndependentReportAsync; the corresponding API delegates to it with IReportSigningCredentialSource.

Correction: document VISUAL versus CERTIFICATE mode, the Required switch, configured-but-invalid refusal, and the exact verification guarantees. Remove revocation/trust claims unless a separately approved and verified implementation exists. Keep production certificate custody and legal acceptance separate.

F06 — High: Microsoft provisioning omits the approved privileged-worker exception

The M365 diagram lists six single-purpose identities, then shows dedicated-site creation and site permission assignment without modeling the provisioner's distinct permissions and isolation. Its general “one permission” description is incomplete for the separately approved site-provisioning resource boundary.

src/AuditSphereOps.Infrastructure/Providers/SharePointClientSiteProvider.cs contains separate SharePoint and Graph resource token sources. SharePoint token validation requires exactly Sites.FullControl.All; the Graph provisioner is also configured for that role. It uses SPSiteManager, verifies the exact ownership marker and site identity, and grants a different document-worker identity write access to the exact site.

docs/architecture/auditsphere-client-sharepoint-sites-current.md confines the privileged credential to the isolated Acceptance client-sites worker, not the API or PBC worker; one role per resource is the relevant exception. Rollout cutoff, consent, configuration and remote verification remain distinct gates.

Correction: model the privileged provisioner explicitly without broadening the ordinary document-worker identity. Preserve Sites.Selected for document operations, the resource distinction, exact-site validation and unknown-create reconciliation. Do not confuse application permissions with Entra directory administrator roles.

F07 — High: Scope authorization is drawn in the wrong layer

The overview and M365 diagrams place scoped RoleGrant enforcement in API authentication middleware.

src/AuditSphereOps.Api/HttpBoundary/HttpPolicies.cs explicitly states that HTTP authorization only establishes an authenticated cookie session. TrustedActorResolver, AuthorizationDecision, RoleGrant scope and business gates remain in Application. The shared endpoint helper re-resolves the session and delegates to named commands/queries; the browser cannot authorize the operation.

Correction: draw OIDC/cookie/CSRF checks at the HTTP boundary and firm/client/engagement/group business authorization inside Application on every read and mutation. Preserve both layers rather than replacing either.

F08 — High: Invoice and release diagrams omit operative finance gates

The onboarding flow says “Issue 50 percent advance invoice”; the release flow assembles the final bundle, then generates its balance invoice. Other document text mentions draft-only automation, but the workflows do not express the full approved dependency and approval boundaries.

src/AuditSphereOps.Application/Practice/AutomaticFeeInvoices.cs implements optional automation which returns without work when disabled. It runs under captured, revalidated finance/administrator authority. It creates drafts through FeeAgreementService.IssueAdvanceInvoiceAsync or IssueBalanceInvoiceAsync. Independent approval, posting and mail dispatch are separate.

The balance discovery condition includes a currently paid advance and a release whose target is a FinancialPackage. A financial-package release and the final five-part commercial bundle must not be collapsed into one event.

Correction: distinguish draft creation, finance approval, posting, dispatch, payment allocation, financial-package release and final bundle assembly. Preserve existing-client exceptions and executed commercial terms. Do not infer automatic posting or a circular final-invoice/bundle dependency.

F09 — Medium: The risk view does not fully incorporate approved current definitions

Historical threshold wording remains useful provenance, but the current view still presents Amber sampling as mandatory and mainly describes banding through balance thresholds.

docs/architecture/adr/auditsphere-architecture-adr-0017-ste-v22-delegated-requirement-decisions-approved.md defines Amber work as Senior-or-above execution and Audit Manager review, with documented senior judgment between sampling and full-population testing; it explicitly rejects a universal sample requirement. It also defines recorded critical-estimate and high-inherent-risk inputs.

src/AuditSphereOps.Application/Audit/RiskBandService.cs records likelihood, magnitude, significance, fraud and critical-estimate inputs, delegates band computation to RiskBandRules.Band, and enforces staffing/independent clearance. It does not take an FSLI balance as the assessment request shown in that path.

Correction: separate historical balance-based requirements from the exact implemented risk-routing inputs and approved product definitions. Any remaining source-versus-code gap requires explicit disposition; do not silently claim equivalence. Show the staffed Engagement Partner requirement for final professional actions, as specified by ADR-0017.

F10 — Medium: Source authority and ADR references remain internally inconsistent

The workflow simultaneously says full accounting/consolidation is implemented and later calls the same capabilities unapproved extensions (around lines 883–898 versus 2051–2056). It also retains “signature technology is open” wording after adding the approved certificate-signing decision. The historical/current boundary is not consistently applied.

Requirements' ADR register contains incorrect baseline references:

Register entry Current reference Problem
ADR-0011 M2.04-R03 This is Revenue; historical normalized PBT is M2.04-R02
ADR-0016 M4.02-R05 This is management correspondence; report/statements are M4.02-R02 and final signature is M4.01-R07
ADR-0005 M4.02-R05 The same correspondence row is not the visual-credentials requirement

Correction: retain historical text but label its applicability at the point of use, and provide the operative overlay immediately beside the affected requirement/diagram. Fix every source reference and link the actual decision document. Do not declare all open professional or external matters resolved by an ADR about a narrower technical choice.

F11 — Medium: Acceptance and design-verification labels are not supported by the matrix

104 cells say only “Satisfies business rule [ID] as defined in source specification §4.” They do not define observable inputs, authorized actor, success result, denial, relevant revision condition or evidence. Copying these cells to a second matrix does not strengthen traceability.

Correction: replace generic cells with focused, testable behavior, appropriate to the requirement's actual granularity. Separately record source authority, design coverage, code implementation and executed acceptance evidence. Some of the historical 115 statements are headings or child bullets; preserve those identities without falsely treating each as a complete independent feature.

Suggested minimum fields: source ID/path/section; current operative rule; actual code path/method or explicit proposed element; API/Angular enforcement path where applicable; one positive criterion; relevant denial/staleness criterion; evidence status and unresolved dependencies.

F12 — Medium: Navigation has improved but extension traceability and runtime validation remain incomplete

The filename-case mismatch is corrected and the canonical cross-document links pass structural checks. Requirements-to-workflow fragments use JavaScript tab routing and are valid; they should not be incorrectly reported as missing DOM IDs.

However, all 23 EXT identifier cells in the workflow are plain spans, despite the instruction that every requirement ID opens its full narrative. Add exact anchors and links for those rows. Deliver the pair using canonical filenames, or consolidate into a single self-contained reference without cross-document file dependencies. If older canonical files sit beside them, navigation can open stale content.

External Tailwind, font and Mermaid dependencies remain in the workflow file. JavaScript syntax checks do not prove Mermaid rendering, CDN availability, mobile interaction or print completeness.

Correction: link extension records, retain explicit network requirements or package local/pre-rendered assets, and execute a focused browser check before claiming interactive or offline acceptance.

Prioritized correction sequence

  1. Remove misleading evidence: quarantine unverified code pointers, eliminate the unsupported implemented/verified claims, and correct the archive and signature contracts.
  2. Establish complete applicable scope: inventory CURRENT v2.2 plus approved extensions/deviations; preserve the original 115 separately. Explicitly identify excluded, proposed and externally blocked items.
  3. Repair source-to-design mappings: use existing application services and exact HTTP/Angular paths; repair security, provider permissions, finance dependencies and risk-policy overlays.
  4. Make acceptance criteria executable: replace generic repetitions; distinguish design coverage from code presence and behavioral verification. Do not retrofit source behavior to incorrect documentation.
  5. Recheck the artifacts: regenerate both views from a common inventory if the existing tooling supports it, preserve source wording and IDs, and run targeted static/browser checks. No full application suite is justified for documentation-only changes.

Acceptance conditions for a subsequent review

The documentation pair can be accepted as a code-aligned reference only when every applicable current requirement has a supported disposition, all concrete code pointers resolve to the reviewed implementation or are explicitly proposed, every diagram preserves actual mandatory gates, and incorrect status/permission/signature claims are removed. A reviewed source commit and observed evidence must remain attributable without duplicating volatile repository state across uncontrolled narratives.

Do not claim 100% production implementation, financial-methodology approval, tenant acceptance or regulatory compliance from these checks. Current deployment, professional and external gates remain governed by their existing records.

Executed versus not executed

Executed: complete local HTML parsing; historical ID/text comparison; matrix equality and status counts; control/state checks; unique-ID checks; route-aware cross-link checks; four node syntax checks; current GitHub snapshot and authority retrieval; targeted source inspection and three source-scoped symbol searches.

Not executed: .NET/Angular builds or application tests; authenticated application journeys; live Entra/Graph/SharePoint operations; database/permission changes; deployed archive/recovery validation; certificate trust/revocation tests; browser execution of the supplied HTML or Mermaid; mobile/print/offline acceptance. These checks are not marked passed.

No source changes: uploaded originals remain unchanged. This report and its validation evidence are separate generated artifacts.

Rendering and verification boundary

The original Mermaid definitions are unchanged and available beneath every architecture view. Flowchart and state visuals are laid out with Graphviz; sequence views use a local SVG renderer. Those offline layouts preserve the parsed nodes, labels, edges and messages, but may look different from Mermaid’s native layout. The HTML does not load or execute Mermaid, a CDN, or web fonts at runtime.

Content counts refer to this source package, not a complete inventory of all approved repository requirements. The v2.2 material included here is explicitly excerpted. No missing domain rules or source-to-code mappings have been invented to force a completion percentage.

Artifact checks: source preservation, internal anchors, SVG integrity, JavaScript syntax, offline loading, navigation, search, zoom and responsive layouts are checked separately from application behavior. No application build, database migration, live provider workflow or repository change is part of this output.
